concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the immunophenotypic profile (CD138-positive, CD56-positive, CD20-negative, PAX5-negative, EBV-positive) and genetic findings (gains of florescence signal at multiple loci), is consistent with Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type.

The patient's immunophenotypic profile (CD138-positive) and genetic findings (gains of florescence signal at multiple loci, including 14q32) could also be consistent with Plasmablastic lymphoma, although the absence of specific markers (e.g. CD20-positive) makes this diagnosis less likely.

The CD20-negative and PAX5-negative findings are unusual for typical B-cell lymphomas, but gains in BCL6 and MYC suggest a possible diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with unusual immunophenotype.
